newsitem.title: USA: Reno - no special probe yet in Clinton funds flap.
newsitem.headline: Reno - no special probe yet in Clinton funds flap.

text.p: U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno said on Thursday that she so far sees no reason to appoint an independent counsel to investigate the fund-raising controversy involving President Bill Clinton.

"As recently as last week, they (Justice Department lawyers) have advised me that it (the evidence in the fund-raising row) does not rise to the standards provided for in the independent counsel statute," Reno said at a news conference. "When it does, I will follow the law of the (independent counsel) statute."

Calls for appointment of an independent counsel in the campaign funds controversy reached a new pitch this week after the White House released documents showing that Clinton had taken an active, enthusiastic role in wooing potential Democratic party backers during the 1996 election campaign.

But Reno said the law required that there be credible evidence a crime had been committed by a high government official, and she made clear she and her advisory staff did not think the evidence against the Clinton administration had reached that level.

"Until then I have got to comply with my responsibilities as the chief law enforcement officer of this country and pursue every allegation as vigorously, thoroughly and fairly as I can," she said at her weekly news conference. "We are going to review the evidence as we develop it and if the evidence triggers the statute (on independent counsel) we are going to ask for the independent counsel."

Reno, who has had frosty relations with the White House because of her willingness to appoint independent counsels to investigate Clinton administration officials, said she was ready to shoulder the responsibility if need be. "If the buck is going to stop with me, let it stop with me," she said.
